get.description: Totals, the latest audit entries and system facts for the admin home.

post.description:
View the app as a user. Read-only unless `mode` is `edit`. Returns a token for that user;
ends any other session you have open.

patch.description:
Switch a session you started between read-only and edit. Takes effect at once, on the
same token.

post.description:
Stop viewing as the user. Works with your admin token or with the view-as token itself;
the view-as token stops working straight away.

delete.description: Go back to the default layout.

put.description: Replace your layout for this scope (order = list order).

get.description:
One card per row of your analytics layout. `on` is today in your time zone. With
`group_share` (the default), your share of group expenses counts as spending in the trend,
categories, daily average, needs and wants and savings rate; the app sends false when its
cash flow leaves the share out.

post.description:
A fresh token for a signed-in user, so people who open the app at least once a week stay
signed in. View-as tokens can't be refreshed: they end with their admin session.

get.description: Home: totals, balance with each friend across groups, and your net in each group.

post.description: Add your own category. Only you see it.

delete.description: Delete one of your own categories, if nothing uses it.
Soft delete. The expense stops counting towards balances and can be restored.

get.description: Who added and changed this expense, oldest first ("Edited by Rahul · ₹1,650 → ₹1,800").
Expenses and payments, newest first, across your groups or within one group.

get.description: Your balance with a friend in each group you share, for the "Settle up" sheet.

post.description:
Settle with a friend across groups: one settlement per group, saved together.

Without `amount_minor` every shared group ends at zero. With it, the payment pays down
the groups owed in its direction, oldest first.

Link a placeholder member (no account) to the account with this email.

If the account exists, the placeholder's expenses, shares and payments in its groups move to
it now. If not, the email is saved as an invite (`invite_email`) and whoever signs up with it
takes the placeholder's place. Everyone's balance stays the same either way.
Record a payment between two members. It never changes any expense.

delete.description: Stop syncing. Nothing is deleted on either side.

get.description:
Whether the group is kept in sync with a tricount, how the last pass went, and the
conflicts waiting for someone to pick a side.

post.description:
Keep this group in sync with a tricount: an existing one (`link`) or a new one made
from the group (`create`). The first pass runs right after; the status says "syncing"
until it's done.

Read a tricount by its share link (without joining it) and suggest who its people are
in this group. Changes nothing.
Sync now instead of waiting for the next pass.

get.description: Your imports, newest first.

post.description:
Remove everything this import created (soft deletes, so items can be restored one by
one). Calling it again changes nothing.

Import the file in one go, as one batch that can be undone.

`options` is JSON: `{"group_id": …}` or `{"new_group": {"name", "currency", "icon"}}`,
plus `people` (`[{"name", "user_id"}]`; no `user_id` makes a placeholder member) and
`categories` (`{"Tricount category": "key"}`; anything unmapped becomes Other).

Read a Tricount export and suggest how to map it. Saves nothing.

`group_id`: import into this group (people are matched against its members).
Otherwise a new group is assumed; `currency` sets its currency (default: the file's).

get.description:
Your accounts, active and closed, oldest first (`deleted=true`: the deleted ones, for
restoring). No balances: the app derives them from each account's opening balance and the
entries in it.

post.description:
In your currency. A repeated id gives back the account it already made. With an
`sms_label`, your entries with that label and no account move into it.

get.description:
The account labels your entries carry, most recently used first, each with the latest
balance its bank reported. Kept until the app stops using `/personal/summary`.

delete.description: Only while no entry is in it (409 `account_in_use`): close it instead.

put.description:
`status: closed` closes it: it takes no new entries and still counts in net worth.
A new `sms_label` moves in your entries with that label and no account.

get.description:
Oldest first (`deleted=true`: cancelled with their income, or deleted). No status: the
app works out planned, partial, fulfilled or cancelled.

post.description:
Usually sent with its income in one `POST /personal/batch`. One plan per income and
rule: the same id gives back the plan, another id gets 409 `plan_exists`.

put.description: A recomputed snapshot and amount (after its income changed).

get.description:
Your rules by priority, then oldest first (`deleted=true`: the deleted ones). Whether
active percentages add up to more than 100% is the app's to say.

post.description:
To a goal that counts contributions or an open account, in your currency. A repeated id
gives back the rule it already made.

delete.description: Its plans stay, but it makes no new ones.

put.description: Fields left out keep their value. Existing plans keep the snapshot they were made with.

post.description:
Up to 100 account and entry creates, updates and entry deletes, applied in order, all or
none. A transfer's two legs go in one batch. A repeated create gives back what it already
made; a stale update gets a 409 and nothing is applied. A refusal says which `item`.

get.description: Newest first, of one goal or all (`deleted=true`: the deleted ones).

post.description:
To a goal that counts contributions. With `transaction_id`, the entry that moved the
money: it counts towards one goal at most, and not if it moves an account a goal follows by
balance (422 `counted_by_balance`).

put.description: `transaction_id` and `note` keep their value when left out.

get.description:
Your goals by priority, then oldest first (`deleted=true`: the deleted ones). No
progress: the app derives it from the source each goal's `tracking_mode` names.

post.description: In your currency. A repeated id gives back the goal it already made.

delete.description: Its contributions go with it, and come back when it's restored.

put.description:
Fields left out keep their value (`status`: null keeps it too). Switching
`tracking_mode` needs that mode's field, and drops the old mode's.

get.description:
Oldest first, of one account or all (`deleted=true`: the deleted ones). No gains or
stale flags: the app works those out.

post.description: In an open investment account of yours. A repeated id gives back the holding it made.

delete.description:
Refused while a live entry names it (409 `holding_in_use`). Its SIP reminders go with
it, and come back when it's restored.

put.description:
"Update value": the valuation is replaced (only the latest is kept). The account,
quantity and cost basis keep their value when left out.

get.description:
By day of the month (`deleted=true`: the deleted ones). No due dates: the app works out
the next one.

post.description: A monthly reminder for a goal or a holding. It never records an entry.

get.description: Your decisions on reminders (`deleted=true`: the ones taken back).

post.description:
Makes the decision for `dedup_key` (201), or replaces the one there is (200), even a
deleted one. Its id is reminder_state_id(you, dedup_key).

delete.description: Takes the decision back: the reminder shows again.

get.description: One month at a glance. `month` is any date inside it (default: this month).

Your own entries (only you see these), newest first, with totals: `spent_minor` is
expenses minus refunds; transfers, adjustments and investments aren't spending.
`reviewed=false&source=sms` is what the app shows as "Just in".

post.description:
Up to 100 entries in one request, all or none. A repeated id (a retry, a bank SMS read
again) gives back the entry it already made, deleted or not.

get.description: The registered split methods, in the order the selector shows them.

post.description: Validate and allocate without saving. Invalid splits return 200 with ok=false.
Changes after your cursors, for every stream you can see, in one call.

get.description: The current state of one stream and the seq it is at. Replace your copy with it.
Entries changed in both apps since they last agreed, in your groups.

post.description:
Keep Splitkit's or Tricount's version. The other app is updated before this returns
(unless Tricount can't be reached; then the worker retries).
